posts.description:
Four wins across two industry awards, and a great moment for all of us at Circles!

We've always believed that the future of telecom can look very different. More digital, more intelligent, more customer-centric, and capable of creating value well beyond connectivity.

That belief has shaped how we've built Circles over the years, and it's rewarding to see the progress we're making recognised by the industry.

First, Circles was named Best AI-Powered MVNO at the MVNO Nation Awards 2026, recognising our push to make AI native to the telco experience, rather than simply another layer of technology.

We then followed that up with three more wins at The Fast Mode Awards 2026!

- Circles – MVNO & Digital Brand Catalyst | Growth
- Circles.Life – AI & Agentic AI Pioneer | Performance
- Jetpac – CX Champion | Performance

What makes these wins particularly meaningful is seeing that ambition translate into real products and customer experiences across our businesses.

Whether it's helping operators around the world launch and scale digital telcos, reinventing the consumer mobile experience through Circles.Life, or making global travel connectivity simpler with Jetpac, we're showing what's possible when we challenge the traditional way of doing things.

It's also a reflection of the industry's broader shift from Telco to Techco, something we've been working towards at Circles from the very beginning.

A huge congratulations to our teams across Circles, Circles.Life and Jetpac! These wins belong to the people who continue to innovate, execute and push boundaries every day.

Thank you to MVNO Nation and The Fast Mode for the recognition!

Excited for what we'll continue to build together, and plenty more to come from all of us at Circles!

posts.transcript: It's 2:00 at Cube Con. The talk you came for is full and so is the hallway. Meet Kathy, a cube scheduler for humans. Rooms are nodes and people are pods. Every capybara here is 10 attendees. When room 155 E fills up, Cappy schedules the overflow filter talks starting now with open seats. Score closest topic, shortest walk, emptiest room bind. Hold the seats so we never send 200 people to a room with 30. The whole decision is 1 elastic search query, a filter and a vector score written in painless. It takes about 10 milliseconds and E SQL counts the demand nobody could see before on your phone. Just asking your own words. Elasticsearch fuses keywords and vectors so something on E BPF and security finds the right talks. Roomful Cappy shows its pick and why one tap and your seat is held while you walk over and with Gina embeddings on Elastic Cloud. You can ask in any language. At a full door, scan the sign. No app, no account. Your Plan B is already there. Prefer somewhere calmer. Quiet mode favors the emptier room. Need a step free route One switch and rooms behind stairs Drop out, hold your seat and Kathy tells you why it fits in one sentence written from the two talks. Elastic search found. Everything is open telemetry IN-01 trace follows a tap from the browser to Elasticsearch and the model. Cappie's mood is our SLO and when search felt slow, Agent 0 found the cause. The embedding call was 92% of the request. We cashed it and 800 milliseconds became 20. It runs on our teams Kubernetes cluster. Argo CD ships every merge and our agent drives it through radars. MCP server. When the first rollout got stuck Radar. Code. Why a private image? Then we ran a radar AI investigation on our app. It traced 2 readiness warnings to our own rollouts. Every deploy took the app down for about 20 seconds. We changed the rollout and measured the next one. One failed request out of 359, and radars checks went from 5 findings to two. Every feature landed through a pull request reviewed by guitar against our own rules. It caught a docker file that would have broken every deploy and fixed it itself. In all, Guitar raised 12 findings and everyone was fixed before merge. A door control anyone could use, a seat held without telling you, and our own rule checks every manifest against the clusters budget. At a real cube con, there's nothing to install. Door staff tap full and the sign has a QR code. Next badges do the counting. One NFC tap at the door and every count is automatic. Organizers size next year's rooms on real demand, not guesses. Cappy Cube, stay chill, Cappy's got your seat.
posts.description:
The Cloud Native Hackathon in Salt Lake City brought us some exciting projects, including CapyKube! 🦫

CapyKube works like a Kubernetes scheduler, but for conference attendees. When a talk reaches capacity, it finds attendees another session that matches their interests, checks walking distance and available seats, and reserves a spot before they arrive.

The project makes heavy use of Elasticsearch for hybrid and multilingual talk search, along with its scheduling engine to find the best alternative sessions. Dash0 powers observability through OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, logs, and browser monitoring. Its Agent0 also helped identify a slow embedding call, bringing search latency down from 857 ms to around 20 ms.

A big thank you to everyone who participated and to our sponsors Elastic, Dash0, Skyhook Radar, and Sonar for making this event possible! 🙌

posts.transcript: Every AI breakthrough comes from years of work most people never see. In 2009, Faye Faye Lee and her team introduced Imagenet. Photos and videos are becoming an integral part of global life. Millions of images carefully labeled. This gave researchers around the world a challenge. Who could build a machine that recognized images most accurately? In 2012, A-Team built a system called Alex Net, far more accurate than any prior method A I learned to understand a cat, a container, a violin. A breakthrough that helped ignite the deep learning revolution and inspired. Generation of AI pioneers and some image net contributors even went on to found open AI shared data helped researchers make breakthroughs. AI learned to understand what but doesn't understand when. Intelligence for the real world, how to deal with high dimensional continuous noisy signal that the real world is, which your house cat is perfectly able to deal with today. All this data is processed at once in a limited context, a snapshot compressed. But the world is not a snapshot. It runs on continuous data heartbeats. A machine vibrating. What happens today can matter tomorrow. This is how the world really works. Every signal is a measurement recorded at a specific time, pieces of a bigger picture. Together they show how things change over time. But this data is scattered across systems, industries and formats. Each measurement captures only one moment. The real intelligence comes from connecting them, seeing patterns, understanding how things change over time. What's missing is a shared foundation to bring them together. Until now. Introducing Time Net 1 Shared Format, a global network of builders contributing data sets with context, linking signals and their interpretation. Imagenet helped AI learn to perceive moments. Timenet lays the foundation for AI to understand how they connect and you can shape what comes next. Bringing temporal AI to life. Time Net.

posts.description:
Saw a post similar to a project I’ve been working on, so I wanted to share.

CourtVision turns a single-camera NBA broadcast into possessions, makes and misses, rebounds and a box score, running locally on a Mac.

How it works:
• Detection: a ResNet-18 CenterNet distilled from RF-DETR looks at 3 frames at once, so a blurred ball still stands out. It runs on Apple’s Neural Engine.
• Court mapping: A broadcast camera only pans, tilts and zooms, so those are the only things it fits per frame.
• Events: a rules engine turns the tracks into possessions, shots and rebounds. A small rim CNN re-judges every make or miss 2.5 s later.
• Decision layer: Jev calls the play type, how big the moment is, and whether each line of Claude’s commentary is backed by the facts. Each call has a deadline of 1.5 s or less and a rule-based fallback.
Live vs recorded:
• Live: 21–30 fps against a 30 fps broadcast on an M3 Pro. Working towards getting it to live level, could probably do it with more compute.
• Recorded: decides possession over the whole game at once, and gets the team with the ball right 97% of the time on held-out footage. The model has only been trained on ~42 games, a few shorter clips.

Code: https://lnkd.in/gcC_J4Da

I am so proud of my friend and collaborator extraordinaire Dr. Joy Buolamwini. The Algorithmic Justice League's 10th year anniversary event was incredible. We got to celebrate AJL's impact with friends and collaborators, learn the stories of people around the world fighting AI harms, and honor them with AJL's Global Justice Awards. This year the recipient was Lindsey Isaacs.

Here's to another decade of impact 🎉 🎉 🎉 

"In October 2025, investigators with the Florida Highway Patrol used footage from automated license plate recognition cameras operated by Flock Safety to identify Isaacs' vehicle near the scene of a crash that killed three people. Despite conflicting witness accounts and a lack of physical evidence linking her vehicle to the crash, Isaacs was arrested in April 2026 on suspicion of vehicular homicide and spent 13 days in jail. Prosecutors subsequently declined to pursue charges against her, and another driver was arrested in connection with the crash.

Since her release, Isaacs has spoken publicly about her experience and called for greater accountability in law enforcement's use of surveillance technology. On Sept. 23, 2026, she testified before the U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism at a hearing examining Flock Safety's nationwide surveillance network. Her testimony highlighted the potentially devastating consequences of relying on AI-powered surveillance data without adequate scrutiny and verification."

https://lnkd.in/g-xVBApz

comments.text:
I agree that the pattern is that more science and more socio-technical application leads to “more human flourishing”. The problem today is that our elites and managerial class are actively hostile to our flourishing. 

On the idea that in the recent past “AI was far behind humans at almost every cognitive task”, but “it is on track to surpass us at almost everything we can do intellectually”, perhaps the __relative__ change is as much – or more – that human intellectualism __has regressed__, and that humanity is under-rated?

We so want to deny our abilities, our learning skills, and our agency that we almost wilfully submit to abstracted “non-human” process, to “the machine”. 

These are three ideas that machine learning could not reach.
comments.author: Nico Macdonald

posts.description:
Last week we hosted Richard Socher of Recursive at the GV (Google Ventures) Ferry Building in San Francisco following the launch of Recursive's first model, Flint, and his new book, Eureka Machine.

The conversation ranged from how to budget compute across parallel research branches to whether AI can be as 'stubborn' as required to do the most difficult and non-obvious things.

Beyond the technical debate, Richard pointed out a simple truth: when we were born, AI was far behind humans at almost every cognitive task: language, reasoning, perception. Within our lifetimes, it is on track to surpass us at almost everything we can do intellectually.

Despite this, people are increasingly worried about AI in our future. Richard’s counter is simple: the future needs better marketing.

If you ask someone how AI changed their life this week, the answer usually feels incremental. But historically, the progression has always held true:

More science → more technology → more economic growth → more human flourishing.

That chain of progress is the reason billions of people can live on this planet today. With AI, the clock speed is tightening.

You can see that acceleration in Recursive's recent launch of Flint. A small team used their automated research system—the Eureka Machine—to build a frontier-class model from scratch in under four months, automating the entire pipeline from tokenizer to post-training.

When Richard and I first discussed recursive self-improvement eighteen months ago, it was a deeply contrarian take. Today, it is reality. When the machine starts building the machine, we are no longer playing a zero-sum game. In fields like life sciences, we are just rapidly expanding the pie.
